books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.text: A black-and-white painting of Sutter's Mill on the American River at Coloma, California: a wooden mill building with a millrace in the foreground, small houses and trees around it, and hills rising behind.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Gold was discovered at this mill in January 1848, and the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo was signed in February 1848. That timing matters most because it means which of the following?

options.text: Mexico knew about the gold and demanded a higher price for California.
options.misconception: News of the gold reached the wider world only months later; Mexico signed without knowing the gold was there.

options.text: The United States acquired California just before the world learned it held gold.
The gold rush began before the Mexican War started.
options.misconception: The war began in 1846 and the gold was found in January 1848, near its end.

options.text: Polk refused to sign the treaty once he heard about the gold.
options.misconception: Polk signed and the Senate ratified the treaty; he announced the gold to Congress in December 1848.

rationales.A: The discovery was known to almost no one outside California when the treaty was signed in February 1848.
rationales.B: Gold was found in January 1848 and the treaty was signed the next month, so the United States bought California before its gold was known.
rationales.C: The war began in 1846; the gold came in January 1848, as the war was ending.
rationales.D: Polk accepted the treaty and later confirmed the gold to Congress in December 1848.
rationales.general:
1. Set the two dates side by side: gold in January 1848, treaty in February 1848.
2. Ask who knew. Almost no one outside California had heard of the gold when the treaty was signed.
3. See the twist. The United States paid $15 million for land that turned out to hold a fortune neither side had counted.
Remember: dates can change a bargain's meaning — California was sold as farmland and bought as a goldfield, though no one knew it yet.
